349.frame: pages 1-4 of 7 (cipher on all; second cipher on p.4)
349.saw: Pages 1-4 are full pages of dense symbol cipher (about 25 lines on p.1); p.4 ends with a block of ~8 lines in a visibly different sign set (letters/Greek-like forms) above the date 'xxxi agosto' and signature. No decipherment written on the pages.
349.note: Page 4 carries the different-looking final passage; pages 5-7 not viewed.

350.saw: English letter, Hague 6 Nov 1648, in clear with inline numeric code groups (e.g. '852.63.42.29.118', '248.404.1037') on the last lines of p.1 and several lines on p.2/3; no decipherment written in.

352.frame: page 1 = f. 92 (clear letter); page 4 = f. 93 (code list)
352.saw: Page 1 f. 92 is clear English with cover names only. Page 4 (f. 93) has an opening line of number groups then two columns of number groups each followed by a cover name (Mr Perkins, Mr Tush ...). Pages 2-3 are verso/blank show-through.

53.saw: Saxon envoy letters in French/German, 1841-43, with long runs of continuous cursive digit strings (no separators, 5-10 lines per block) inside the clear text; R5005 p.1,3,4 are mostly cipher pages, p.2 letter of 10 Jan 1841 with 7 lines; R5006 p.1 has 8 cipher lines, p.2 3 lines; R5007 p.2 about 10 lines; R5008 p.1 2 lines, p.2 3 lines. No decipherment on the pages.

70.saw: BL Add MS 32305: pure three-digit number code in lines, no decipherment on the sheets. R2968 'Anonyme a Carre, Mars 1742' sheets a-d; R2970 'Copie d'une lettre en chiffre' to Carre, sheets A-D (+E); R2972 letter dated Lond. 19 Janv. 1745, 4 pages.

76.frame: page 1 (f. 1), page 2 (f.1v/2), page 3 (f. 2) ; page 4 sealed verso
76.saw: Numeric code of 3-4 digit groups joined with hyphens, ~30 lines on p.1 (small slip), ~30 on p.2, ~25 on p.3 ending 'Duplicata'. No decipherment.

77.frame: page 1 = f. 37 (cipher), page 3 = f. 38 (frequency list), page 4 (sign tables)
77.saw: Symbol cipher in ~9 lines of dotted cursive signs on f. 37; f. 38 is an analysis sheet (signs with frequency counts, crossed out, 'Duplicata') and p.4 a sign table; no plaintext written on them.
77.note: 8 pages in record; only first 4 viewed.

78.frame: R2964 pp.1-2 (Paris 7 Nov 1719), R2965 pp.1-2 (Paris 10 Feb 1719)
78.saw: Letters in French (extracts) in numeric code groups of 2-3 digits, with the decoded words (que, vous, le, re, a, +) written above numbers: partially glossed. Both records fully cipher pages.

123.saw: Letter-book copies of Walsingham to Burghley, Jan 1572, all clear English; the text mentions a 'cypher' but no cipher characters on the three pages.

128.saw: Burghley/Walsingham letter-book (Harley 260), Sept 1571: clear English and Latin; on p.4 a short run of cipher signs inserted in the text (about one line near the bottom, after 'you truly 3367') plus struck words. Pages 1-3 clear only.
128.note: Cipher is a few signs only; pages 5-6 not viewed.

161.saw: German letter dated 22 (?) 1635 with long runs of symbol cipher (square, plus, hash-like signs) filling most lines, clear German interspersed in the lower lines; page 2 is blank binding/edge shot.

169.frame: page 1 (f. 63r, cipher words), page 4 (zodiac table); ms. 74 images
169.saw: Italian alchemical manuscript (Mellon 29): p.1 has a line and paragraphs of substituted words in a lettered cipher (e.g. 'qgghsio rshu ...') and zodiac names encoded; p.4 is a table 'Ariete si chiama ... Taurus ...' with the cipher word for each sign. p.3 has a clear Italian preface (dated 1315/1492).
